blocks.body: A contact starts with listening. Foundations Lab 02 is the radio. Lab 03 is the repeater. This lab is the order of the actions. No microphone is required.

config.doneText: You heard the other contact, left that frequency, listened again, called, and identified.

steps.prompt: You want to call a friend. The radio is already on a frequency.
steps.heard: Two stations are in the middle of a conversation.
steps.success: You listened first. The frequency is busy.
steps.hint: Find out whether anyone is there before you transmit.

steps.heard: The same two stations are still talking.
steps.success: You moved. Covering their contact would not get you a clear frequency.

hints.TRANSMIT: They are using the frequency. Calling on top of them is interference, not a contact.
hints.WAIT: Waiting is polite if you need this exact frequency. This step is to leave a busy one.
hints.IDENTIFY: Identification does not make it acceptable to transmit over an ongoing contact.

steps.prompt: The new frequency might be clear. Check.
steps.heard: You have not listened on the new frequency yet.
steps.success: It is quiet. Now you know the frequency is available in this model.
steps.hint: A new frequency still gets a listen.

steps.success: You placed the call on a frequency you had just checked.
steps.hint: The frequency is clear. Make the call.

steps.prompt: Finish the call with your call sign.
steps.success: The other station can tell who called.
steps.hint: A call without your call sign is not a finished identification.

blocks.body: Set the handheld the way Lab 02 taught, spell a call sign with phonetics, then set microphone gain and look at two filter widths.
A repeater contact, then a net that asks you to wait, then a test. QSY in the hint means change frequency. You do not need a list of Q-signals.

config.doneText: You listened on the repeater, called, identified, waited for the net, and identified the test.

steps.prompt: You want a repeater contact. Check the output first.
steps.success: Quiet. A silent key-up would still be a transmission.
steps.hint: Listen on the output before you transmit.

steps.prompt: Call. Include who you are calling and your call sign in the next steps.
steps.success: The call is going out on the input. The repeater, if it accepts you, will retransmit it.

hints.ADJUST: Tone and offset matter, and they are settings from Lab 03. This step is the call itself.
hints.IDENTIFY: Say the call as you transmit. Press TRANSMIT to place the call, then identify before you finish.

steps.prompt: Put your call sign on the transmission.
steps.heard: Your carrier is up on the repeater input.
steps.success: The repeater users hear your call sign, not only the repeater's tail.

steps.prompt: A net control says: stand by, emergency traffic only.
steps.heard: Net control: emergency traffic only. Please stand by.
steps.success: You waited. A net is directed. Emergency traffic takes the channel.

hints.TRANSMIT: The net control asked stations to stand by. Your routine call can wait.
hints.CHANGE FREQUENCY: Leaving is possible, but the asked action is to wait.

steps.prompt: The net control says the channel is open for a short radio check.
steps.heard: Net control: short radio checks are welcome.
steps.success: The test carries your call sign. A test is not an excuse to transmit without identification.
steps.hint: A radio check is still your transmission. Identify it.

blocks.prompt: Why should you listen before transmitting on a frequency?
blocks.reference: Someone may already be using the frequency. Listening tells you whether to wait, move, or call. Transmitting first can cover a contact you did not know was there. On a repeater, listening to the output tells you whether the machine is busy before you key the input.
blocks.unsure: Go back to the first frequency. The conversation was already there. The listen button is what revealed it.

blocks.body: RADIO LAB PRACTICE. These questions are about the contacts you just made. They are not official exam questions.

blocks.label: RADIO LAB PRACTICE
blocks.notice: Original practice about the contacts you just made. Not official exam questions.

questions.stem: A frequency might be busy. What did this lab have you do first?
choices: Transmit a short call and apologize if someone answers
Change frequency without listening, because a move is always safe
questions.why: The first action on the busy frequency was LISTEN. Moving came after you heard the contact.

questions.stem: You have listened and the frequency is quiet. What belongs in the call?
choices: Only the word hello, with the call sign saved for later
The repeater's call sign instead of yours
questions.why: The station identification is your call sign. Phonetics can clarify the letters. They do not replace the call sign.

questions.stem: The repeater output is quiet. Which action matches this lab?
choices: Key the radio in silence to see if the tail beeps
Turn the squelch to zero and transmit over whatever you then hear
questions.why: A repeater contact is still listen, then transmit, then identify. A silent key-up is a transmission without identification.

questions.stem: Net control has asked stations to stand by for emergency traffic. What do you do with a routine call?
choices: Play a long tone so net control knows you are there
questions.why: A directed net gives the channel to the traffic it named. Your routine call waits.

questions.stem: The other station says your voice is loud and distorted. What did the gain control show?
choices: Turn the microphone gain down from the high setting
Open the filter wider, because gain and bandwidth are the same knob
questions.why: High gain distorted the voice. Usable gain was understandable. The filter is a separate control.

questions.stem: Someone says QSY. What is the beginner meaning used here?
questions.why: QSY is a short way to say change frequency. You do not need a long list of Q-signals to use that one.

blocks.body: You are at a trailhead. Make one basic contact. Listen before you call.

config.doneText: You left the busy frequency, listened on the clear one, called, and identified.

steps.prompt: The radio comes up on a frequency as you reach the trailhead.
steps.success: The net is using this frequency.
steps.hint: Listen before you decide to call.

steps.prompt: You do not need to join that net.

hints.TRANSMIT: The net is busy. Move rather than calling over it.

steps.prompt: Check the simplex frequency you planned with your friend.
steps.success: 146.520 MHz is quiet in this model.
steps.hint: Listen on the new frequency too.

steps.prompt: Close the call so the other station knows who you are.
steps.success: The trailhead contact included your call sign.
